```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

In our first empirically calibrated simulation we simply permuted the treatment assignment labels to create new datasets (with no treatment effect).
In those simulations we found that the estimated standard errors would be systematically too high or too low across permutations.
We wanted to assess whether this was a finite-sample property of the individual datasets, and thus made a new simulation where we generated data according to the distribution of cluster and block sizes, along with a few other descriptive statistics.

In these simulations, we are generating entirely new datasets with each iteration, so are adhering to a superpopulation model rather than a finite population one.



```{r, include=FALSE}

# Analyze the fingerprint simulations calibrated to the empirical
# data.  These are NOT the rerandomization simulations, but the ones
# based on the summary statistics.

library( clusterRCT )
library( tidyverse )
library( cli )

# Load study index and some listed core methods ----

core.methods <- c("LRa-FE-db", "LRa-FIcw-db", "LRapw-FE-db", "LRapw-FIpw-db", "MLM-FE", "MLM-FIcw", "MLM-RE")


core.methods.se <- c("LRa-FE-db", "LRa-FE-het", "LRa-FIcw-db", "LRapw-FE-db", 
                     "LRapw-FE-het", "LRapw-FIpw-db", "LRapw-FIpw-het", 
                     "LRicw-FE-crve", "LRicw-FIcw-crve", "MLM-FE", "MLM-FIcw",
                     "MLM-RE")


studies = read_csv( here::here( "empirical/results/study_descriptions.csv" ),
                    show_col_types = FALSE )
studies <- filter( studies,
                   blocked == "Blocked" )
studies



# Load and examine data ----

cli_h1( "!!! Loading and examining results" )

if ( FALSE ) {
  
  # Read one example result file
  res = read_rds( here::here( "fingerprint/results_fingerprint",
                              paste0( studies$UniqueID[1], ".rds" ) ) )
  res
  table( res$runID )  
}


dat <- studies$UniqueID %>%
  set_names() %>%
  map( \(file) {
    fname = here::here( "fingerprint/results_fingerprint", paste0( file, ".rds" ) )
    # check if file exists
    if ( file.exists( fname ) ) {
      read_rds( fname )
    } else {
      NULL
    }
  } )  %>% 
  bind_rows( .id = "UniqueID" )

dim( dat )
dat
table( dat$runID )
length( unique( dat$runID ) )


# Who is missing?
missing_sets <- setdiff( studies$UniqueID, dat$UniqueID )
filter( studies, UniqueID %in% missing_sets ) %>%
  dplyr::select( UniqueID, n, J )

dat <- left_join( dat, select( studies, UniqueID, Collection ),
                  by = "UniqueID" )



studies <- filter( studies,
                   UniqueID %in% unique( dat$UniqueID ) )

# Calculate ranges, etc. ----

range_dat <- dat %>%
  group_by( Collection, UniqueID ) %>%
  nest() %>%
  mutate( data = map( data, summarize_simulation_results, "cross" ) ) %>%
  unnest( data ) 


ranges <- range_dat %>% 
  rename( group = weight ) %>%
  group_by( group, runID ) %>%
  summarise( mn_rngATE = mean( rangeATE ),
             sd_rngATE = sd( rangeATE ),
             prob_10p = mean( rangeATE > 0.10 ),
             mn_ratSE = mean( ratioSE ),
             prob_2x = mean( ratioSE >= 2 ),
             sd_ratSE = sd( ratioSE ),
             mn_naATE = mean( na_ATE ),
             sd_naATE = sd( na_ATE ),
             mn_naSE = mean( na_SE ),
             sd_naSE = sd( na_SE ),
             n = n(),
             .groups = "drop" )

sub_dat <- range_dat %>% 
  ungroup() %>%
  filter( runID %in% sample( unique( ranges$runID ),  5 ) )

sub_dat

# Distribution of ATEs for all methods across studies
if ( FALSE ) {
  ggplot( dat, aes( UniqueID, ATE_hat ) ) +
  geom_jitter( size=0.25, width=0.1, height=0 ) +
  coord_flip()
}
```





```{r}
ggplot( sub_dat, aes( rangeATE ) ) +
  facet_grid( weight ~ runID ) +
  geom_dotplot( method="histodot", binwidth = 0.02 ) +
  labs( title = "5 replicates of fingerprint for ATE range" ) +
  theme_minimal()

summary( sub_dat$ratioSE )
sub_dat$ratioSE[ sub_dat$ratioSE > 5 ] = 5
ggplot( sub_dat, aes( ratioSE ) ) +
  facet_grid( weight ~ runID ) +
  geom_dotplot( method="histodot" ) +
  labs( title = "5 replicates of fingerprint for SE ratio",
        subtitle = "(Ratios windsorized at 5x)" ) +
  theme_minimal()


# Calculate method performances ----

table( dat$method, useNA="always" )

meth_dat <- dat %>%
  group_by( Collection, UniqueID ) %>%
  nest() %>%
  mutate( data = map( data, summarize_simulation_results, "method" ) ) %>%
  unnest( data ) %>%
  ungroup()

meth_dat  

nrow(studies)
nrow(meth_dat) / nrow(studies)

# Are the estimators SE estimates variously unstable? ----



# Each method estimate for each study
table( meth_dat$method )

meth_dat <- meth_dat %>%
  group_by( UniqueID ) %>%
  mutate( cal = ESEhat / SE,
          rel_SE = SE / median(SE, na.rm=TRUE),
          stab = sdSEhat / median(SE, na.rm=TRUE) ) %>%
  ungroup()


ggplot( meth_dat, aes( method, cal )) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs( title = "Calibration of SE estimates",
        subtitle = "Ratio of estimated SE to true SE" ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  geom_hline( yintercept = 1 ) 



ggplot( meth_dat, aes( method, rel_SE )) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs( title = "Method true SE to median true SE within study" ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  geom_hline( yintercept = 1 ) 



ggplot( meth_dat, aes( method, stab )) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs( title = "sd(SE-hat) / median(SE)" ) +
  theme_minimal()



filter( meth_dat, UniqueID == "TRIADScale-up_rema2" ) %>%
  dplyr::select( -c( UniqueID, Collection, weight, biased ) ) %>%
  knitr::kable( digits = 2 )




# Looking at true SEs for person vs cluster weighting ----

wts <- meth_dat %>%
  group_by( Collection, UniqueID, weight ) %>%
  summarise( meanSE = mean(SE, na.rm=TRUE),
             sdSE = sd(SE, na.rm=TRUE), .groups = "drop" )

ggplot( wts, aes( UniqueID, meanSE, col=weight ) ) +
  facet_wrap( ~ Collection, scales="free" ) +
  geom_point( size=1, position=position_dodge(width=0.5) ) +
  geom_errorbar( aes( ymin=meanSE-sdSE, ymax=meanSE+sdSE ),
                 width=0.2, position=position_dodge(width=0.5),
                 alpha=0.5 ) +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_minimal()
```



# Which studies tend to have high ratios, etc?

```{r}
rng <- range_dat %>% 
  mutate( ratioSE = pmin( ratioSE, 5 ) ) %>%
  group_by( Collection, UniqueID ) %>%
  summarise( across( rangeATE:na_SE, list( mn = mean, sd=sd,
                                           Q95 = \(x) quantile(x,0.95),
                                           Q05 = \(x) quantile(x,0.05) ) ),
             .groups = "drop" )

ggplot( rng, aes( UniqueID, rangeATE_mn ) ) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_errorbar( aes( ymin=rangeATE_Q05, ymax=rangeATE_Q95 ),
                 width=0, alpha=0.5 ) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs( title = "Mean rangeATE across studies",
        subtitle = "Range of ATEs for each study" ) +
  theme_minimal()



ggplot( rng, aes( UniqueID, ratioSE_mn ) ) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_errorbar( aes( ymin=ratioSE_Q05, ymax=ratioSE_Q95 ),
                 width=0, alpha=0.5 ) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs( title = "Mean ratioSE across studies",
        subtitle = "Range of ATEs for each study" ) +
  theme_minimal()

range_dat$ratioSE[ range_dat$ratioSE > 5 ] = 5
range_dat$UniqueID = fct_reorder( range_dat$UniqueID, 
                                   range_dat$ratioSE, 
                                   .desc = TRUE )

ggplot( range_dat, aes( UniqueID, ratioSE ) ) +
  facet_wrap( ~ Collection, scales="free_y" ) +
  geom_boxplot( fill="grey", outlier.size=0.3 ) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs( title = "ratio of SEs across simulation runs",
        subtitle = "Windorizerd at ratio of 5" ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_y_log10()
```

We see the ratio of SE across methods heavily depends on the average cluster size:
```{r}
rd = left_join( rng, studies, by="UniqueID" )
rd
ggplot( rd, aes( Jbar, ratioSE_mn ) ) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  geom_smooth( se=FALSE, span=1, method="loess" ) + 
  geom_point()+
  theme_minimal() +
  labs( title = "Typical ratio of SEs across methods",
        subtitle = "Windorizerd at ratio of 5",
        x = "Average cluster size (Jbar)",
        y = "Mean ratio" )
```

We next look more closely at studies where Jbar was less than 4.3:

```{r}
range_dat = left_join( range_dat, studies, by="UniqueID" )
sb <- filter( range_dat, Jbar < 4.3 ) %>%
  mutate( UniqueID = fct_reorder( UniqueID, Jbar, .desc = TRUE ) )

rd %>% 
  arrange( Jbar ) %>%
  filter( Jbar < 4.3 ) %>%
  dplyr::select( UniqueID, J, Jbar, K, ratioSE_mn, rangeATE_mn, na_SE_mn ) %>%
  unique() %>%
  print( n = 15 )

ggplot( sb,
        aes( UniqueID, ratioSE ) ) +
  geom_boxplot( fill="grey", outlier.size=0.3 ) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs( title = "ratio of SEs across simulation runs",
        subtitle = "Studies with Jbar < 4.3; Windorizerd at ratio of 5" ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_y_log10()
```
